1	# RTK — Token-Optimized Commands
2	
3	## Golden Rule
4	
5	**Use `rtk` for any command whose output may exceed a few lines.** Inside WSL Remote sessions the global PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites Bash commands to their `rtk`-prefixed form (`git status` → `rtk git status`). On native Windows shells the hook is unavailable, so prefix explicitly. `rtk` passes through commands without a dedicated filter unchanged — always safe to use.
6	
7	```bash
8	# ✅ Correct (chains too)
9	rtk git add . && rtk git commit -m "msg" && rtk git push
10	```
11	
12	## Commands by Category
13	
14	```bash
15	# Git
16	rtk git status / log / diff / show / add / commit / push / pull / branch / fetch / stash
17	
18	# GitHub CLI
19	rtk gh pr list / view / create
20	rtk gh issue list / view
21	rtk gh run list
22	
23	# Build & Type Check
24	rtk tsc                  # TypeScript errors only, grouped by file
25	rtk lint                 # ESLint grouped by rule/file
26	rtk next build           # Next.js build compact
27	
28	# Tests
29	rtk test <cmd>           # generic — failures only
30	rtk vitest / jest / pytest / cargo test / go test
31	
32	# Files & Search
33	rtk ls <path>            # token-optimized tree
34	rtk read <file>          # smart file read
35	rtk grep <pattern> <path>
36	rtk find "*.ext" <path>
37	rtk diff <a> <b>
38	
39	# Containers
40	rtk docker ps / images / logs / compose ps / compose logs
41	rtk kubectl pods / logs / services
42	
43	# Data & Errors
44	rtk json <file>          # structure without values
45	rtk err <cmd>            # filter errors only from any command
46	rtk log <file>           # deduplicated log
47	rtk env -f <prefix>      # filtered env vars
48	rtk curl <url>           # truncate + save full output
49	
50	# Meta
51	rtk gain                 # token savings stats
52	rtk gain --history       # recent commands
53	rtk gain --daily         # day-by-day breakdown
54	rtk discover             # find missed savings opportunities
55	rtk init --show          # verify which AI tool integrations are active
56	```
57	
58	## When to Use
59	
60	Wrap any noisy command (`git`, `docker`, `tsc`, test runners, `find`, log files). Skip for commands that produce only a handful of lines. RTK passes through unknown commands transparently.
